question: You have completed a structured assessment of a 12-year-old obese boy. Findings include: BMI 30.2 kg/m² (98th percentile on IAP 2015 charts), acanthosis nigricans on the neck and axillae, and blood pressure 128/82 mmHg (>95th percentile for age, sex, and height). Which interpretation and documentation priority is most appropriate?

answers.text: Document BMI only; acanthosis nigricans and elevated BP are common cosmetic and incidental findings in obese children and do not require further investigation.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Acanthosis nigricans is a skin marker of insulin resistance, and BP >95th percentile indicates paediatric hypertension — both are significant metabolic comorbidities of obesity that require structured investigation and documentation, not dismissal.

answers.text: Classify as obesity (BMI-for-age ≥95th percentile); document acanthosis as a marker of insulin resistance requiring metabolic workup (fasting glucose/HbA1c); and classify BP >95th percentile as paediatric hypertension requiring further evaluation.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This child has obesity (BMI ≥95th percentile on IAP 2015), acanthosis nigricans indicating insulin resistance (warrants fasting glucose or HbA1c), and paediatric hypertension (BP >95th percentile for age/sex/height). Structured documentation of each comorbidity guides the management plan.

answers.text: Refer immediately for bariatric surgery since BMI is above the 95th percentile with two comorbidities.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Bariatric surgery in paediatric patients requires very specific indications (typically BMI ≥35 with severe comorbidities in adolescents). A 12-year-old with two metabolic markers needs structured investigation and lifestyle management first, not immediate surgical referral.

answers.text: The BMI must be re-measured in 6 months before any documentation or management plan, since a single measurement is unreliable.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A single BMI-for-age measurement at ≥95th percentile with comorbidity markers (acanthosis, hypertension) is actionable. Waiting 6 months without any intervention or documentation is clinically inappropriate.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each finding must be interpreted in its paediatric context: BMI-for-age (IAP 2015) for obesity grade, acanthosis nigricans as insulin resistance marker, and paediatric BP thresholds (not adult 140/90) for hypertension classification.

Correct. Structured interpretation documents each finding in its clinical context: obesity classification by BMI-for-age, acanthosis as insulin resistance marker, hypertension by age/sex/height-adjusted thresholds.
